Effect.summary: Effect represents one effect instance applied to a layer (e.g. a Gaussian Blur applied to a footage layer). The MatchName identifies the effect type ("ADBE Gaussian Blur 2", "ADBE Gradient Wipe", etc.) and Parameters holds each tweakable knob as a Property. Parameter match-names are internal numeric suffixes like "ADBE Gaussian Blur 2-0001".

Folder.summary: Folder is a project panel folder.

Footage.summary: Footage represents a source media file, an AE solid, or a placeholder.

Footage.AssetType.summary: AssetType returns the footage kind as a string: "placeholder" / "solid" / "file". Mirrors py-aep's `footage.asset_type` discriminator. Footage items with neither flag default to "file".

Footage.Comment.summary: Comment / Label — Item-level metadata (project-panel comment + timeline color chip). Populated by parseItem from the cmta + idta chunks under the Item LIST.

Footage.EndFrame.summary: EndFrame returns the footage end frame (sspc @0xB0, uint32 BE). 0 for non-sequence footage and for fixtures without a full-size sspc.

Footage.File.summary: File returns the footage source file path. Empty string for solids and placeholders. Alias of [Footage.Path] for py-aep API parity.

Footage.FootageMissing.summary: FootageMissing reports whether the footage source file was missing at the time AE saved the project (per the `footage_missing_at_save` flag in sspc @0x78). Solids and placeholders never have a file, so this is always false for them (regardless of the on-disk flag bit).

Footage.HasAudio.summary: HasAudio reports whether the footage has an audio stream — true when sspc's audio_sample_rate (8 byte f64 BE at @0xA0) is non-zero. Solids and placeholders never have audio.

Footage.IsPlaceholder.summary: IsPlaceholder is true when opti tag = "Plac" (AE's placeholder footage — name + dimensions only, no source file). Mutually exclusive with IsSolid and with having a non-empty Path.

Footage.IsSolid.summary: AE solid (generated solid-color source); solids have no disk path

Footage.IsStill.summary: AE flagged this as a still image

Footage.ItemID.summary: ItemID returns the footage's item id (mirrors the ID field). Provided so *Footage satisfies AVItem.

Footage.ItemName.summary: ItemName returns the footage's name. Provided so *Footage satisfies AVItem.

Footage.MainSource.summary: MainSource returns the typed source metadata for this footage item. Returns *FileSource for file footage, *SolidSource for solids, *PlaceholderSource for placeholders. Returns nil if the footage was built outside the parser (no source chunks available).

Footage.Name.summary: display name; SetPath syncs this to the new path's basename

Footage.Path.summary: source file path on disk; empty for solids/placeholders. Writable via SetPath

Footage.SetComment.summary: SetComment writes a project-panel comment on the footage item. Length-variable; same semantics as Composition.SetComment.

Footage.SetLabel.summary: SetLabel writes the project-panel color label index for the footage.

Footage.SetPath.summary: SetPath updates the footage's source path. The change is propagated to the underlying RIFX chunks (the alas JSON's "fullpath" field is rewritten in-place; a legacy Cpth chunk, if any, is fully replaced). The next call to Project.WriteAEP will serialize the new path.

Footage.StartFrame.summary: StartFrame returns the footage start frame (sspc @0xAC, uint32 BE). 0 for non-sequence footage and for fixtures without a full-size sspc.

FromReader.summary: FromReader parses an .aep file from an io.ReadSeeker.

InterpType.summary: InterpType identifies a keyframe's interpolation mode on one side (in-side or out-side). AE stores these as single-byte enums in the keyframe block at offsets 0x04 (in-interp) and 0x05 (out-interp).

Keyframe.summary: Keyframe represents a single keyframe on a property.

Keyframe.FrameTime.summary: FrameTime returns the keyframe's time as an integer frame count (Time × owning-comp FrameRate, rounded). Returns 0 when the keyframe was built outside the parser (FrameRate unknown).

Keyframe.InSpatialTangent.summary: length 3 when present; nil for non-spatial

Keyframe.InTemporalEase.summary: length 1 for spatial+1D, length N for non-spatial N-D

Keyframe.SetFrameTime.summary: SetFrameTime writes the keyframe's time from an integer frame, delegating to SetTime. Returns an error when the owning comp's FrameRate is unknown.

Keyframe.SetInInterp.summary: SetInInterp / SetOutInterp write a new interpolation enum byte to the keyframe block @0x04 / @0x05. length-preserving (1 byte).

Keyframe.SetInSpatialTangent.summary: SetInSpatialTangent / SetOutSpatialTangent write 3D Bezier tangent vectors. Only valid for spatial properties (Position / AnchorPoint with motion path enabled). Slice length must equal `Property.Components`. length-preserving (dims × 8 bytes).

Keyframe.SetInTemporalEase.summary: SetInTemporalEase writes a new per-side temporal ease list to the keyframe. The slice length must match the keyframe's current ease shape:

Keyframe.SetOutTemporalEase.summary: SetOutTemporalEase mirrors SetInTemporalEase for the out side.

Keyframe.SetTime.summary: SetTime rewrites this keyframe's time in-place using its owning composition's TickRate (decoded at parse time from cdta). Chunk size does not change, so writing the project back never relocates anything.

Keyframe.SetValue.summary: SetValue rewrites this keyframe's numeric value in-place.

Marker.summary: Marker represents a single timeline marker on a layer (or a comp). Times are in seconds. The remaining string fields hold the user- editable annotation data (most are empty unless the user filled them in inside AE's "Marker Dialog").

Marker.Comment.summary: first Utf8 in the Nmrd block

Marker.Duration.summary: seconds; 0 = point marker. Decoded from NmHd @0x08 / 600.

Marker.FrameDuration.summary: FrameDuration returns the marker's duration as an integer frame count. 0 for point markers (Duration == 0).

Marker.FrameTime.summary: FrameTime returns the marker's time as an integer frame count.

Marker.Label.summary: timeline label color index (0..16); 0 = default. NmHd @0x10.

Marker.Remove.summary: Remove deletes this marker from its owning composition / layer marker set.

Marker.SetChapter.summary: SetChapter rewrites the marker's chapter-link text (second Utf8 in the Nmrd block).

Marker.SetComment.summary: SetComment rewrites the marker's primary comment text (first Utf8 child of the Nmrd block). length-variable — the Utf8 chunk's data slice is replaced wholesale; WriteAEP recomputes ancestor LIST sizes.

Marker.SetCuePointName.summary: SetCuePointName rewrites the marker's cue-point name (fifth Utf8 — legacy Flash-era; rarely populated in modern AE projects).

Marker.SetDuration.summary: SetDuration writes a new marker duration (seconds) to NmHd @0x08. Encoded as uint32 BE in 600ths-of-a-second per py-aep documentation; see decodeNmHd doc comment for the offset rationale. length-preserving (4 bytes).

Marker.SetFrameDuration.summary: SetFrameDuration writes the marker's duration from an integer frame.

Marker.SetFrameTarget.summary: SetFrameTarget rewrites the marker's frame-target id (fourth Utf8).

Marker.SetFrameTime.summary: SetFrameTime writes the marker's time from an integer frame.

Marker.SetLabel.summary: SetLabel writes a new timeline label-color index (0..16) to NmHd @0x10. Indices outside 0..16 are written verbatim (AE shows index 0 for unknown values but the byte round-trips). length-preserving (1 byte).

Marker.SetTime.summary: SetTime writes a new marker time (seconds) to the ldat keyframe slot using the owning composition's TickRate. length-preserving.

Marker.SetURL.summary: SetURL rewrites the marker's web-target URL (third Utf8).

Marker.Time.summary: marker position in seconds, decoded via the owning composition's TickRate

Mask.summary: Mask represents a single vector mask on a layer. Each mask has a closed or open path made of Bezier vertices.

Mask.Color.summary: R, G, B from mkif @0x2D-0x2F (timeline label color)

Mask.Feather.summary: Other mask-level properties, populated when their cdat values exist in the mask atom's property tree. Feather is 2D (X, Y) in pixels; Opacity is 0..1; Expansion (AE's "Mask Expansion", internally "ADBE Mask Offset") is in pixels.

Mask.Index.summary: from mkif @0x08 (AE internal mask ID, not always sequential)

Mask.Locked.summary: from mkif @0x01 (== 1 when AE timeline UI lock is on)

Mask.MkifRaw.summary: 48 bytes raw mask info (preserved for write-back)

Mask.PathKeyframes.summary: nil when path is not animated

Mask.Properties.summary: Properties is every other tdmn+tdbs leaf inside the mask atom's property group (anything beyond Shape/Feather/Opacity/Offset, or those when keyframed). Useful for keyframed mask properties (e.g. animated feather).

Mask.SetClosed.summary: SetClosed toggles whether the (first) path is closed (shph @0x14). length-preserving (1 byte). For animated masks this only affects the first snapshot; per-keyframe closed flags aren't exposed yet.

Mask.SetColor.summary: SetColor writes the mask timeline label color RGB to mkif @0x2D/@0x2E/@0x2F. AE always keeps alpha (0x2C) at 0xFF; this setter does not touch it. length-preserving (3 bytes).

Mask.SetInverted.summary: SetInverted toggles the mask Inverted flag (mkif @0x00). length-preserving (1 byte).

Mask.SetLocked.summary: SetLocked toggles the mask's lock flag (mkif @0x01). When locked, AE refuses edits to the mask in the timeline UI; the bytes are still mutable through this library. length-preserving (1 byte).

Mask.SetMaskMotionBlur.summary: SetMaskMotionBlur writes the per-mask motion-blur override at mkif @0x02. Valid values: MaskMotionBlurSameAsLayer (0), MaskMotionBlurOn (2), MaskMotionBlurOff (3). length-preserving (1 byte).

Mask.SetMode.summary: SetMode writes a new mask Mode enum (uint32 BE) to mkif @0x04. length-preserving (4 bytes).

Mask.Vertices.summary: first snapshot (or only one when static)

MaskMode.summary: MaskMode is the compositing mode for a mask (matches AE C++ SDK values).

MaskMotionBlurMode.summary: MaskMotionBlurMode describes the per-mask motion-blur override. AE's MaskMotionBlur enum uses these stored values:

MaskPathKeyframe.summary: MaskPathKeyframe is one keyframe of an animated mask path. Time is in seconds. Vertices is the full path snapshot at that time. Easing follows the same scalar (one TemporalEase per side) layout as spatial keyframes.

MaskVertex.summary: MaskVertex is one Bezier control point along a mask path. Coordinates are stored as ABSOLUTE positions (not offsets from the anchor):

NewProject.summary: NewProject returns a fresh empty Project parsed from the embedded AE skeleton matching the requested target.

Open.summary: Open parses an .aep file by path and returns the Project.

Project.summary: Project holds the fully parsed contents of an .aep file.

Project.AVItemByID.summary: AVItemByID returns the *Composition or *Footage with the given id, or nil if no AV item in the project matches (or id == 0). Folders are not AV items and are not consulted.

Project.AudioSampleRate.summary: AudioSampleRate returns the project's audio sample rate in Hz. Returns 0 when the adfr chunk is absent or too short.

Project.ColorManagementSystem.summary: ColorManagementSystem returns the color management system used by the project. Returns ColorManagementSystemAdobe (0) when CMS chunk is absent.

Project.CompensateForSceneReferredProfil.summary: CompensateForSceneReferredProfiles reports whether AE compensates for scene-referred profiles when rendering (acer byte 0 != 0). Returns false when the chunk is absent.

Project.CompositionByID.summary: CompositionByID returns the first composition whose ID matches id, or nil if no such composition exists. ID 0 is treated as no-match (mirrors Composition.LayerByID; real AE projects start item IDs at 1). Footage and Folder items share the same ID namespace but are stored in separate slices, so an ID belonging to a non-composition item returns nil here.

Project.CompositionByName.summary: CompositionByName returns the first composition whose Name matches the given string, or nil if none does. Matching is exact (case-sensitive). Comp names aren't guaranteed unique in AE; use CompositionByID when you need precise identity.

Project.DisplayStartFrame.summary: DisplayStartFrame returns the display start frame (0 or 1). This is derived from frames_count_type % 2. Returns 0 when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.DuplicateComposition.summary: DuplicateComposition deep-clones src (a comp in this Project) as a new sibling comp named name, appended to p.Compositions. The dup contains a fresh copy of every layer (new layer IDs), with intra-comp parent + track-matte refs remapped to the dup's own layers; layer SOURCES (footage / precomp items) are shared verbatim, not duplicated — matching AE ScriptingAPI's CompItem.duplicate(). Returns the new *Composition.

Project.EffectNames.summary: EffectNames returns the match-names of every effect referenced by the project, from the root-level `Pefl` LIST → `pjef` Utf8 entries. Returns nil when the project has no Pefl LIST (e.g., projects with no effects applied anywhere or builder-synthesized projects).

Project.ExpressionEngine.summary: ExpressionEngine returns the project's expression engine name ("extendscript" or "javascript-1.0"). Defaults to "extendscript" when the ExEn chunk is absent — matches py-aep's behavior.

Project.FeetFramesFilmType.summary: FeetFramesFilmType returns the film type for feet+frames timecode display. Returns FeetFramesFilmTypeMM35 (0) when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.FootageByName.summary: FootageByName returns the first footage item whose Name matches the given string, or nil if none does. Matching is exact (case-sensitive).

Project.FootageTimecodeDisplayStartType.summary: FootageTimecodeDisplayStartType returns how timecode is displayed for footage. Returns FootageTimecodeDisplayStartTypeStart0 (0) when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.Footages.summary: Footages returns the project's footage items (alias of the Project.Footage slice field, named to match py-aep's `project.footages` for API parity).

Project.FramesCountType.summary: FramesCountType returns how frames are counted in the project. Returns FramesCountTypeStart0 (0) when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.FramesUseFeetFrames.summary: FramesUseFeetFrames returns whether frames use feet+frames display. Returns false when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.GpuAccelType.summary: GpuAccelType returns the project's GPU acceleration device id (UUID-style string inside the gpuG LIST → Utf8 child). py-aep models this as a labeled enum; we surface the raw string since AE writes a runtime-resolved device UUID. Empty string when the chunk is absent.

Project.LayerByID.summary: LayerByID searches every composition in the project for a layer with the matching ID and returns the first hit. Returns nil for id == 0 (the "no layer" sentinel) and when no comp owns this id. Mirrors py-aep's `project.layer_by_id(id)`.

Project.LinearBlending.summary: LinearBlending reports whether the project uses linear blending (presence of lnrb chunk under root).

Project.LinearizeWorkingSpace.summary: LinearizeWorkingSpace reports whether the working color space is linearized for blending (presence of lnrp chunk under root).

Project.LutInterpolationMethod.summary: LutInterpolationMethod returns the LUT interpolation method. Returns LutInterpolationMethodTrilinear (0) when CMS chunk is absent.

Project.MarshalJSON.summary: MarshalJSON serializes the Project as JSON.

Project.NewComposition.signature: func (p *Project) NewComposition( name string, width, height uint16, frameRate, duration float64, ) (*Composition, error)
Project.NewComposition.summary: NewComposition adds an empty composition to the project's root folder.

Project.OcioConfigurationFile.summary: OcioConfigurationFile returns the OCIO configuration file path. Returns empty string when CMS chunk is absent.

Project.RenderQueue.summary: RenderQueue holds the parsed render queue (LIST:LRdr). Nil when the project has no LRdr chunk; non-nil with empty Items for an empty queue. Read-only (P3 §3A slice-1).

Project.Revision.summary: Revision returns the project's file revision counter — incremented by AE on each save. Read-only here since the head chunk also carries the next-item-id counter that our writer manages independently. Returns 0 when the file has no head chunk or its data is too short.

Project.RootFolder.summary: RootFolder returns the project's root folder. AE projects always have a root folder at the top of the items tree; we return the first Folder slice entry, or nil when the project was built without folders (synthesized minimal fixtures).

Project.SetAudioSampleRate.summary: SetAudioSampleRate writes the adfr f64 BE. Refuses unknown rates outside AE's UI-supported set.

Project.SetBitsPerChannel.summary: SetBitsPerChannel writes the project's color depth (8 / 16 / 32 bpc) to BOTH the nhed @0x0F and nnhd @0x18 header bytes. AE stores the enum redundantly; we keep both in sync.

Project.SetColorManagementSystem.summary: SetColorManagementSystem sets the color management system. Rejects values other than the defined enum members.

Project.SetCompensateForSceneReferredPro.summary: SetCompensateForSceneReferredProfiles writes the acer byte. Refuses when the acer chunk is absent (no slot to mutate; AE 23+ writes it by default — files without it are rare).

Project.SetDisplayStartFrame.summary: SetDisplayStartFrame sets the display start frame (0 or 1). This modifies frames_count_type to preserve the value.

Project.SetExpressionEngine.summary: SetExpressionEngine writes the ExEn Utf8. Refuses values other than "extendscript" / "javascript-1.0" — matches py-aep's validator.

Project.SetFeetFramesFilmType.summary: SetFeetFramesFilmType writes the film type to nnhd byte 8, bit 7.

Project.SetFootageTimecodeDisplayStartTy.summary: SetFootageTimecodeDisplayStartType writes the timecode display start type to nnhd byte 9.

Project.SetFramesCountType.summary: SetFramesCountType writes the frames count type to nnhd byte 20.

Project.SetFramesUseFeetFrames.summary: SetFramesUseFeetFrames writes the frames_use_feet_frames flag to nnhd byte 11, bit 0.

Project.SetGpuAccelType.summary: SetGpuAccelType replaces the gpuG Utf8 string in-place (length-variable splice; WriteAEP recomputes parent LIST size).

Project.SetLinearBlending.summary: SetLinearBlending toggles the lnrb chunk under root.

Project.SetLinearizeWorkingSpace.summary: SetLinearizeWorkingSpace toggles the lnrp chunk under root.

Project.SetLutInterpolationMethod.summary: SetLutInterpolationMethod sets the LUT interpolation method. Rejects values other than the defined enum members.

Project.SetOcioConfigurationFile.summary: SetOcioConfigurationFile sets the OCIO configuration file path.

Project.SetTimeDisplayType.summary: SetTimeDisplayType writes the time display type to nnhd byte 8, bits 6-0.

Project.SetTimecodeDefaultBase.summary: SetTimecodeDefaultBase writes the timecode default base to nnhd bytes 14-15.

Project.SetTransparencyGridThumbnails.summary: SetTransparencyGridThumbnails writes the transparency grid thumbnails flag to nnhd byte 25.

Project.SetWorkingGamma.summary: SetWorkingGamma writes the dwga selector byte. Refuses values other than 2.2 and 2.4 (AE's only UI options).

Project.TimeDisplayType.summary: TimeDisplayType returns how time is displayed in the project. Returns TimeDisplayTypeTimecode (0) when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.TimecodeDefaultBase.summary: TimecodeDefaultBase returns the default timecode base (1-999). Returns 0 when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.ToJSON.summary: ToJSON converts the Project to a JSON-serializable view.

Project.TransparencyGridThumbnails.summary: TransparencyGridThumbnails returns whether transparency grid is shown in thumbnails. Returns false when nnhd chunk is absent.

Project.Warnings.summary: Warnings collects non-fatal parsing anomalies — chunks whose header looked sane enough to attempt decoding but whose payload did not match the expected layout (length mismatch, impossible counts, etc). Each entry is a human-readable string; the parser keeps going and produces a best-effort Project. Empty (nil) on a clean parse.

Project.WorkingGamma.summary: WorkingGamma returns the working gamma value (2.2 or 2.4) per the dwga byte 0 selector (0 → 2.2, non-zero → 2.4). Returns 2.2 default when dwga is absent.

Project.WorkingSpace.summary: WorkingSpace returns the working color space name (R only). Returns "None" when the chunk is absent or has no baseColorProfile.

Project.WriteAEP.summary: WriteAEP serializes the (possibly mutated) project back to RIFX binary form. Sizes are recomputed from the current chunk data, so mutations such as Footage.SetPath that change byte lengths are handled correctly.

Project.WriteJSON.summary: WriteJSON writes the project as indented JSON to w.

Project.XmpPacket.summary: XmpPacket returns the project's XMP metadata packet (trailing UTF-8 XML after the RIFX root chunk). Returns "" when the file has no XMP trailer or the project was built outside the parser.

Property.summary: Property represents an animatable layer property.

Property.Active.summary: Active is an alias for Enabled — mirrors py-aep's `property.active` which returns `self.enabled`. Kept as a separate accessor for parity even though it's a thin wrapper.

Property.CanVaryOverTime.summary: CanVaryOverTime reports whether AE will accept keyframes on this property. Most properties can; group containers and some metadata-only properties cannot. Read from tdb4 @0x0B bit 1.

Property.Components.summary: 1 for scalar, 2 for 2D point, 3 for 3D point, etc.

Property.ControlType.summary: ControlType returns the UI control type for the property (scalar slider, color picker, angle dial, etc.). Derived from tdb4 flags.

Property.DefaultValue.summary: DefaultValue is the property's default value (what AE considers the "unmodified" state). For transform properties, set from hardcoded tables during parse; for effect parameters, from pard chunks. nil when unknown (non-transform, non-effect properties).

Property.DeleteKeyframe.summary: DeleteKeyframe removes the keyframe at index i from the property's ldat stream and decrements the lhd3 count header. Returns an error when i is out of range or the property has no keyframe stream.

Property.DimensionsSeparated.summary: DimensionsSeparated reports whether a multidimensional property has its dimensions split into separate per-axis followers (AE's "Separate Dimensions" on Position). Read from tdsb byte 3 (_enable_flags) bit 1; defaults to false when the tdsb chunk is absent. Only the leader (the "ADBE Position" property) carries this flag set. W (the structural separate/merge toggle) is deferred — it restructures the property group.

Property.Elided.summary: Elided reports whether the property is hidden from the AE UI. py-aep sets this for parser-synthesized placeholder groups; we don't synthesize anything yet, so this always returns false. Reserved for future implementations that materialize missing slots.

Property.Enabled.summary: Enabled reports whether the property is enabled (UI toggle next to the property name in AE's timeline). Read from tdsb byte 3 bit 0; defaults to true when the tdsb chunk is absent — matches py-aep's `TdsbChunk._enable_flags` default of 1.

Property.Expression.summary: JS expression source, "" when no expression set

Property.ExpressionEnabled.summary: tdb4 @0x78 inverted: false = AE ignores expression at render time. Always true for properties without an expression (AE's default state)

Property.Gradient.summary: Gradient holds the parsed gradient data for "ADBE Vector Grad Colors" properties. The XML is stored in the cdat chunk and parsed during property initialization. nil for non-gradient properties.

Property.InsertKeyframe.signature: func (p *Property) InsertKeyframe(time float64, value any) (*Keyframe, int, error)
Property.InsertKeyframe.summary: InsertKeyframe builds a new bpk-byte keyframe block and inserts it into the property's ldat stream, then updates the lhd3 count header. Returns the new Keyframe and its index in Property.Keyframes (insertion is time-sorted; ties land after existing keys at the same time).

Property.IsAnimated.summary: IsAnimated reports whether the property has keyframes. When the tdb4 chunk is available it reads the explicit animated flag (byte 0x44 bool); otherwise it falls back to len(Keyframes) > 0.

Property.IsColor.summary: IsColor reports whether the property is a color (RGBA). 4-channel color properties like Fill Color, Tritone Highlights/Midtones/Shadows. Read from tdb4 @0x3B bit 0.

Property.IsInteger.summary: IsInteger reports whether the property is integer-valued (some dropdowns / enum knobs). Read from tdb4 @0x3B bit 2.

Property.IsModified.summary: IsModified reports whether the property has been changed from its default state. A property is considered modified when it has keyframes, has an expression (regardless of enabled state), or its StaticValue differs from DefaultValue. Mirrors py-aep's `Property.is_modified` minus the always-modified special-cases (Source Text, mask-index, effect-NoValue) which depend on parser context we don't yet track.

Property.IsNameSet.summary: IsNameSet reports whether the property has an explicit display name set (different from its match-name). Currently a thin proxy: `Name != "" && Name != MatchName`. py-aep checks the underlying tdsn Utf8 chunk; our parser doesn't yet decode tdsn into Property.Name (always defaults to MatchName), so this returns false for parsed properties until tdsn decode lands.

Property.IsNoValue.summary: IsNoValue reports whether the property has no stored value (group-like properties, dropdown markers). Read from tdb4 @0x39 bit 0.

Property.IsSeparationFollower.summary: IsSeparationFollower reports whether the property is a per-axis component of a separated multidimensional property (X / Y / Z Position).

Property.IsSeparationLeader.summary: IsSeparationLeader reports whether the property is the multidimensional leader that can be separated into per-axis followers — true for "ADBE Position" regardless of whether it is currently separated (use DimensionsSeparated for the actual state). Mirrors py-aep.

Property.IsSpatial.summary: IsSpatial reports whether the property is spatial (motion-path) — Position and Anchor Point are spatial; Scale / Rotate / Opacity are not. Read from tdb4 @0x05 bit 3.

Property.IsVector.summary: IsVector reports whether the property is a vector type — multi-axis point properties like Position, Scale. Read from tdb4 @0x3B bit 3.

Property.LastValue.summary: LastValue is the property's last-set value from the pard chunk (effect parameters only). nil for non-effect properties.

Property.LockedRatio.summary: LockedRatio reports whether the property's locked ratio flag is set. Read from tdsb @0x02 bit 4 (py-aep: byte 2 bit 4 = locked_ratio).

Property.MaxValue.summary: MaxValue returns the maximum permitted value for the property, or nil if no tduM chunk is present.

Property.MinValue.summary: MinValue returns the minimum permitted value for the property, or nil if no tdum chunk is present. Type depends on property kind: float64 for scalars, []float64 for multi-component, float64 (from uint32) for integer properties.

Property.NbOptions.summary: NbOptions is the number of options for enum/dropdown effect parameters (pard chunk). 0 for non-enum properties.

Property.ParentGroup.summary: ParentGroup returns the AEPropertyGroup that contains this property in the layer's hierarchical property tree, or nil when the property was built outside the parser, lives inside an Effect/Mask (not the layer-level tdgp), or hasn't been wired through wirePropertyTreeLeaves.

Property.PropertyDepth.summary: PropertyDepth returns the number of levels of parent groups between this property and the containing layer. Returns 0 for top-level property groups (Transform, Effects, etc.), 1 for their direct children, and so on. Returns -1 when the property has no parent tree group wired up.

Property.PropertyIndex.summary: PropertyIndex returns the 0-based position of this property within its parent AEPropertyGroup, or -1 when the property has no parent group (i.e. was built outside the parser or is a top-level item).

Property.PropertyMatchName.summary: PropertyMatchName returns the property's AE match-name (e.g. "ADBE Position"). Implements PropertyBase.

Property.PropertyName.summary: PropertyName returns the property's display name. Implements PropertyBase.

Property.SeparationDimension.summary: SeparationDimension returns the axis a separation follower represents (0 = X, 1 = Y, 2 = Z), or -1 when the property is not a follower. (-1 stands in for py-aep's None.)

Property.SetDimensionsSeparated.summary: SetDimensionsSeparated toggles AE's "Separate Dimensions" on a Position leader. Alpha / structural. Both directions (separate↔merge) are implemented for static AND animated Position; an animated leader routes to the keyframe-stream migration paths (separatePositionAnimated / mergePositionAnimated), both ship-gated AE 2020+2025.

Property.SetExpression.summary: SetExpression rewrites the JavaScript expression source attached to this property.

Property.SetExpressionEnabled.summary: SetExpressionEnabled toggles whether AE evaluates the property's expression at render time (separate knob from `SetExpression` which writes the JS source itself).

Property.SetLockedRatio.summary: SetLockedRatio sets the locked ratio flag on the property. Writes to tdsb @0x02 bit 4 (length-preserving).

Property.SetStaticValue.summary: SetStaticValue rewrites a property's constant value in-place (only valid for properties without keyframes — those with a cdat chunk).

Property.UnitsText.summary: UnitsText returns the text description of the units for the property (e.g. "pixels", "degrees", "percent", "seconds", "dB"). Returns "" when the property has no known unit.

Property.ValuePropertyType.summary: PropertyValueType returns the type of value stored in the property (OneD, TwoD, ThreeD, Color, NoValue, etc.). Derived from tdb4 flags.

TemporalEase.summary: TemporalEase is one side's temporal ease for one component:
